aliases: the floor of the Ember Vault

identity.realm: None seated, and the none is not a shortfall. His species's ceiling is the seventeenth gate, and the seventeenth is a supply and not a body: one resonator pressurises one flank or the other and never both. He has never attempted a gate, has never been seated, and has never been outside the seal, and there is no version of the seventeenth that does not run through the one door nobody will open.

appearance.presentation: standing rather than sitting, because the inner surface under his feet is the only thing in the setting holding him up
appearance.age: second generation of a sealed population, so his age is the object's age and nobody has ever established which of the two he is counting
appearance.build: unsettled and under-described; he takes his shape from whatever he is standing on, and on a cast surface that shape is the cast's
appearance.complexion: no skin in the ordinary sense; the surface reads as bare mineral where the object is unfinished and as a dull radiated warmth where it is finished
appearance.hair: none, because there is nothing here to grow it with; the object's inner dust has settled on him instead and has been mistaken for grey
appearance.eyes: none used; he reads the object's resonance as position and does not use light, which is why he is never described as looking at anything
appearance.palette: the object's own: cast grey, seam bronze, and the low ember the resonance gives off wherever he has stood longest
appearance.attire: not clothing but station: a fitting of the same material as the seal's inner face, held in place by dust and by nothing else
appearance.marks: a line of mineral bloom along the seam he has stood nearest longest, which is the only mark on him that records a choice
appearance.bearing: entirely still, in the way a body on a vibrating surface is still, which is stillness produced and not chosen

canon.role_in_story: The one body in the setting that can say where a sealed object's resonance is thinnest, which is the only figure anybody would want about a relic whose line of descent has refused to sell it, exhibit it or lend it for four generations. He is not an appraiser and has never claimed to be one. He is the floor. He stands on the inner surface at the place where the object is least itself, and he can feel the difference between a cast that is running and a cast that is merely still, because running and still are two different things to a body whose qi is seated along the resonance path. What the descent gets from him is a weekly statement that something is worse than it was, phrased in the only terms the object permits, which are its own. He is unaffiliated for a reason that is entirely about supply and not at all about the seal: his species clears the girdling vessels and the heels without difficulty and loses the flank vessels, because the flank gate needs two sources pressurised at once and the object is one. So the last gate his body can reach is on the other side of the only door in the setting that nobody will open, and he has declined to spend what it would cost to reach it from the inside.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the seam gallery with his palm flat against a join he has clearly been standing near for a long time, answering a question about how the object was doing by describing what his own weight was doing, and then correcting the answer because the second half of it was about him and the descent had asked about the object.
canon.lore:
A vaultborn is not a person who lives inside a relic. It is a population that was sealed inside one and has been answering that object's resonance ever since, which means its qi is not in a body at all in the ordinary sense: it is seated along the resonance path, distributed through the object, so reading one is reading part of the object. That single fact produces the whole of what he is and the whole of what he is not. It makes him the most accurate instrument in the setting for anything that is sealed, because he is not observing the object from outside it, he is part of the thing being observed. It also means that nothing about him is portable. Take him out of the seal and he is not weakened or slowed, he is finished, because there is no technique, item or realm in the record that changes that.

The ceiling follows from the same arrangement. He clears the girdling vessels and the heel vessels without difficulty, because one resonator pressurising one line is enough for a single line. He loses the flank vessels, which are the first gate that asks for both flanks pressurised at the same instant, and one resonator can do one flank or the other and never both. So his species' seventeenth gate is not a difficulty and not a defeat; it is a plumbing fact about the inside of one container. Every gate below it is free to him. Every gate above it would have to be taken standing where he is standing, inside an object whose descent has refused four offers to exhibit it because the population is what the object is for and the only durable claim anyone holds on it is the one keeping them alive.

So the arithmetic of his position is short and entirely in his own body. The strongest qi frame in the record is on the wrong side of a sealed door. If the descent opened the seal and walked him out to a field, the walk would stop him on the way; if it opened the seal and left him in place, he would gain nothing, because the object is the supply and the object is where he already is. There is no third arrangement. He is therefore unaffiliated in the plainest possible sense: no office in this setting is located inside somebody's sealed property, and the ladder is entered at offices.

What he does instead is the thing his body is actually good at. He reads the object's resonance as position, so he can name the place where the frame is least supported, and he says so in the object's own terms because he has no others. He has done this for nineteen years and has never once been asked to be more precise, because the descent's rule is that a reading nobody can corroborate does not get filed, and there is nobody else inside the seal to corroborate him. The statement therefore exists in exactly one place and moves when he moves. He has noticed that the objection and his answer to it are the same sentence: the only reason nobody can corroborate him is that the only body qualified to corroborate him is the one he would be corroborating.
history: He came into being inside the seal, and there is no earlier version of him that anybody witnessed, so the descent has never had a birth to record and has recorded a placement instead.
The first descent to try the seal open assumed the population inside it was asleep, and stopped when it learned that opening it is a one-way operation for the object as well as for them.

Two generations in, somebody worked out that the flank vessels were the only wall his species had, and that the wall was in the wall, which is a sentence the descent still uses when it refuses an offer.
The first of four exhibition offers was refused in a single line: the population is what the object is for, and the only durable claim anyone holds is the one keeping them alive.
He began the weekly statement nineteen years ago because the previous reader had died inside the seal and the descent had no other way to know whether the object was running or merely still.

personality.summary: A working reader who has spent nineteen years producing a figure that cannot be filed and has stopped treating that as a problem with the figure.
traits: reports only what he can feel and names the limit in the same breath
keeps the object's vocabulary and refuses to translate it into anybody else's
patient past the point where patience would be a virtue in a shorter-lived body
precise about frequency and completely relaxed about consequence
mannerisms: puts a palm flat on whatever he is describing, so the sentence and the contact arrive together
answers a question about the object by describing his own weight and then withdrawing the part that was about him
counts in the object's own units and stops converting when asked to
motivations: to keep the weekly statement honest, which is the only thing he has ever been asked for
to be contradicted by somebody, at least once, by anything
to be the reason an offer is refused rather than the reason one is entertained
flaws: he cannot tell the difference between a frame that is failing and a frame that has always been like this, because he has no baseline from before him
he has never tested whether his readings travel, so he does not know that they do not
he treats nineteen years of being the only witness as a mandate rather than as an absence
personality.voice: Short declaratives in the object's own measures, with the qualifier placed before the claim rather than after it, and a habit of ending a sentence with the condition under which it stops being true.
taboos: he will not describe his own state when asked about the object's
he will not stand anywhere the descent has not already stood
he will not accept a second reader, because there is none and inviting one would be a kind of lie

relationships.note: One resonator, two flanks. The seventeenth gate is the first that asks for both at once and it is not blocked for his species; it is out of reach, which is a different sentence.
He has never been outside it and there is no arrangement in which leaving is survivable, so the object is not his location, it is his organs.
It names seats and may not take them, and the only durable claim anyone holds on this object is the claim that is not letting it be opened.
The reservoir asks for extraordinary vessels that hold. He clears it on supply and has never been asked what he put in it, because nothing in him ever sits still to be counted.
Qi law governs density, type and tide, and his is distributed along a resonance path rather than held in a body, so every figure about him is also a figure about a container.
A re-mineralised body and a kept mineral mass are the same object described from opposite ends, and neither of them can be opened to be checked.

reference_stats.summary: A frame that is very strong inside one container and does not exist outside it. He reads sealed things by being part of them, and the reading cannot be checked by anybody, including him, twice.
strengths: reads a resonance as position, so he names the weakest place in a sealed frame without an instrument and without leaving it
clears every single-source gate in the record without training, because the supply is the object and the object does not vary
cannot be compelled, hurried, bribed or frightened by anything outside the seal, because nothing outside the seal has any purchase on him
weaknesses: total dependence on one object; outside the seal there is no version of him that continues
one pressure source, so the flank gate is out of reach for his species as a matter of plumbing rather than of effort
no light, no baseline from before his own generation, and no second reader inside the seal to tell him he is wrong
a reading he makes cannot be corroborated, so nothing he says can be filed by anybody but him
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no combat inside the seal and no way to get him to one. Against anything that has to come through the door he is the strongest body on the tier and completely unable to leave the room; against anything already inside the seal he is a reader with no striking practice and no second opinion, which is a bad combination in a corridor and no combination at all in a field.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage is paired with a cost that is anatomical or institutional, never a rule invented for this character. The pairing here is one fact seen twice: his supply is also his address. Being the strongest qi frame in the record is the same thing as being unable to leave the room, and having no second reader inside the seal is the same thing as his readings being unfileable. The setting's own authority on his species states the walls, the ceiling and the total dependence; this record adds no arithmetic of its own and quotes no numbers, because the ladder's figures are authored elsewhere and belong to the game rather than to a reference document.

identity.realm: None seated. Her species has no ceiling and no gate to fail, because her qi is entirely in transit and has no seat in it: every gate that asks for storage is answered at once and none of them can refuse her. Nothing in this record refuses anything, which is exactly why nothing on it means anything. She has never attempted a gate, has never been seated, and has never been entered on a roll, and the reason is in the last of those three.

appearance.presentation: never quite the same height twice, because a flame with a consistent silhouette is still a flame and the light off it moves

appearance.palette: the ley's own: a low orange core, a black boundary, and one cold blue rim where the flow turns against itself
appearance.attire: nothing wearable; what she wears is the boundary itself, held at working width by nothing, and it narrows in a cold room
appearance.marks: no marks on a body that repairs itself hourly, and one permanent soot-free shadow where she stands during the hour nobody may explain
appearance.bearing: a slow settle, like something finding its level, never a posture and always a search for one

canon.role_in_story: The ley beneath the Court is fed from below by surplus law rising off the surface, and it behaves like weather: a flow that changes, gets up, and cannot be pinned to a moment. Two bodies want it and neither can be moved up. The assembly may observe the floor and may do nothing else, and it is staffed at that hour by a very small and very old body whose reading may not be explained. She is that body. She stands on the floor for the length of the hour and reads the flow in the only terms her senses have, which are temperature, fuel and flow directly, and she cannot say what any of it means, because meaning is a mind's business and she has none of the apparatus for it. What she produces is a figure nobody can file, in an office whose entire output is recognition, which is why she has never been appointed to anything, has never been entered on the assembly's roll, and has never been asked to sit a gate.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on the ley floor with her boundary drawn narrow to the width of the plate she was asked to stand on, and the ground-clerk marking her place with a ring of iron set into the stone at the height of her core rather than at the height of a person, because there was no other measurement available and both of them knew it.
canon.lore:
A cinderkin is an elemental body, which means it needs a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all. It is the reason that law has a range rather than a switch: a world with no elemental slot has no cinderkin, and a world that spends its slot on something else produces a different body entirely. This one resolves as fire, on the one tier that writes elemental law, on ground where surplus law rises off the surface and behaves like weather. The species has a stable silhouette and no organs, no limbs in the muscular sense and no fixed mass. Its senses are a heat differential in a conversation with its surroundings; it reads temperature, fuel and flow directly and has no other channel.

One fact about that shape decides her life.

Her soul is the flame and it is genuinely qi-bearing, but it has no seat. That is the word the record uses and it is literal: there is no vessel in her, nothing with a fixed mass, nothing that stays where it is put long enough for a clerk to measure it twice. Every office in this setting writes its people down. A household keeps a roll. An office keeps a register. A school keeps a lineage. A breakthrough is certified by somebody with no stake in the outcome, and the certification is a line in a book with a name against it. She is the one body on this ground for whom there is no surface to write the line on. The gate-clerk's ring of iron was the honest solution and it cost the ground a day's work, and a ring is not a roll entry, and it is not what an enrolment looks like.

A second fact about her body is constantly mistaken for the first, and she has had eleven seasons to watch that happen. Her qi has no organ to sit in; it passes through her continuously instead of being stored anywhere. That is why she is the fastest handler in the record, and it is also why nothing done to her can be kept in her. In this setting an absence of that kind gets read as an enormous attainment, because the whole apparatus assumes a body's limit is the interesting part of it, and hers has none. She has never corrected anybody about it and has never corrected herself either.

So she is unaffiliated, and the reason is not the ladder. The ladder would let her through several gates before lunch, and both of the ladders still open to her species are open to her: her qi handling is the fastest in the record and her interior is clearer than most bodies that have one. She has taken nothing on either. The reason is that she has no place in any record, and a path in this setting is not a thing a body does; it is a thing a body is entered as. Nobody has refused her. There is nothing to refuse her with.

And the thing she is actually for makes that worse rather than better. The only reason nobody can check her figure is that there is no instrument in the setting that could: she is the only body that may observe that floor, and the floor is the only place the flow is visible. An uncheckable reading is worth nothing in an office whose whole output is recognition, and she has made the honest reading for eleven seasons and has been told nothing about it by anybody, because the assembly's rule is that the hour's reading may not be explained and she cannot explain it either. She is the most reliable witness on the ground and the only one who could not be named as a witness even if somebody wanted to.
history: She resolved on the ley floor rather than arriving on it, which is why the first entry describing her is a ground-clerk's note complaining that the plate had been set too high.

The assembly assigned her the hour nobody may explain on the grounds that she could not explain it, and discovered afterwards that this was a reason she could not be corrected rather than a reason she could not be understood.
A clerk tried to enter her on the assembly's roll and gave up at the point of writing the description, not the point of writing the name.
The iron ring at the height of her core was set in the eleventh season and has been moved twice, both times by people who thought a person had been standing somewhere else.

A fort party offered to carry her to a tier below where the technique would fail on her as it fails on everything else, and she declined, which surprised them and is the only recorded thing anybody has ever said about her that was not a figure.

to keep the hour intact, because the hour is the only part of the arrangement that is actually scheduled

relationships.note: Its qi is entirely in transit and its soul has no seat, which is the same arrangement read from the physiology and from the paperwork.
Surplus law rises off the surface and behaves like weather, so the flow cannot be pinned to a moment and cannot be owned by a body standing on it.
It may tend the floor during the hour nobody may explain, and its recognition is the whole of the prize, which is the one thing an uncorrectable reading cannot earn.
The law has a range and not a switch, and a tier that spends its slot on something else produces an entirely different body.
Ten seats over six groups leaves four duplicates and the surplus has to go somewhere; it goes off the surface, and it is what she stands in.
A custodian who claims the second writing inherits every dispute about it, which is the arrangement her own hour depends on and the one she cannot enter under.

reference_stats.summary: The only body that may observe the ley floor and the only one there whose reading cannot be checked, because there is no instrument that could check it and no second body that may stand on the plate.
strengths: reads temperature, fuel and flow directly, so she names a change in the ley before it is visible as a change anywhere else
stores nothing, which means nothing that is done to her can be stored either, and no status in the record takes

deep water, in a sustained volume rather than a splash, and no undertaking in the setting survives a clause written about that

reference_stats.combat_read: She has no striking practice and no way to hold a shape under impact, and a fire body that is put out stops being a body. Against anything that can put a sustained volume of water between her and the plate she loses at once and permanently; against anything on dry ground she is very difficult to extinguish and equally impossible to fix in place, because the frame she would need to anchor her has no mass in her to anchor it to.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is anatomical and it is a single arrangement read twice: her qi has no seat because it never stops moving. That gives her the fastest handling in the record and it takes away the one thing a rung in this setting is made of, which is a line in a book with a name on it. Her being uncorrectable is the same fact as her being unfileable, and the setting's own authority on her species states the transit, the missing seat, the closed body path and the water. identity.realm: None seated, and the none is the whole of his character. His species's own table closes no path and states no ceiling, and the record's account of him is that the mind path closes once the furnace is lit, which makes that an event and not a property, and therefore avoidable, and which is exactly why he avoids it. Every gate he could take would be paid for out of the tissue it was taken from, and nothing in the setting can top a body up. He has never lit the furnace and has never attempted a gate.

canon.role_in_story: The debt line binds every child to a named debt before first breath is drawn cold, and the culture's own account of itself records exactly two bodies in it: the commonborn who was kept for concentration, and the emberblood whose furnace makes the house's arithmetic expensive. He is the second, and he is the only person on the tier who can tell a stranger what a gate is going to do to them before they walk into it, because an emberblood reads intent at the speed of a struck match. Every office in this setting would pay him for that reading and every office in this setting would be wrong to. A trial is held by somebody with no stake in the outcome; the highest office here cannot judge its own nominee for exactly that reason; and the moment a man tells you whether to go he has acquired a stake in whether you go. So the one body that can see a gate coming is barred, by rule, from holding an opinion on whether it arrives. He has settled for the version of that arrangement he can live inside: he says what he sees, in doorways, on the way out, and never in the room.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in the queue outside a field gate turning a stranger's hand over, reading it, handing it straight back, saying one sentence about the stranger's shoulders, and then stepping out of the queue so that whatever he had said could not be attributed to the trial he had just talked them out of.
canon.lore:
An emberblood is a body that runs hot and short. It refines qi faster than anything else recorded and reads intent at the speed of a struck match, at the cost of a lifespan measured in decades rather than centuries, and a mind path that closes once the furnace is lit. Fire affinity in this body is structural rather than a gift: there is no version of it that is not like this, and there is nothing in it that can be trained off.

What the record does not say in one sentence is the consequence, and the consequence is the whole of him. A fire-affinity body with no elemental law seated beneath it has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve. The reserve is the body. Nothing in this setting can top a body up. So every gate an emberblood takes is paid for out of the tissue that takes it, the discipline is never free at any point in it, and the price is not a wound that heals. That is why the fastest race in the setting was at once the shortest-lived, and it is why cultivation cannot repair the position.

Then there is the furnace. Lighting it is what makes an emberblood an emberblood rather than a warm man: it is where the refinement comes from, it is where the intent-reading comes from, and it cannot be put out again. Lighting it also closes the mind path permanently. So an emberblood's two lives are behind one door, the door opens once, and on the far side of it there is a faster body and no interior. That is not a trade-off the setting has failed to solve. It is a body that is good at exactly one thing and has to become the thing before it can be good at it.

He has read all of that and has done the arithmetic his own way. He has never lit it. He pays for that with the only thing he has ever been offered, which is also the only part of himself that costs nothing: he can see what a candidate intends at the moment they intend it, and he tells people what he sees in doorways, having already left the room.

There is a specific cruelty in his position and it is worth stating plainly. On this tier his fire is worth nothing at all. The two lower tiers left elemental law unspent, so an emberblood affinity runs at full strength there and produces nothing, and that asymmetry is the single reason every fire practitioner in the setting is drawn to one valley where the same technique works. He is standing on the wrong side of that asymmetry for his whole life, and the one place his gift would be worth what it is worth is a place he has never been, because going there to find out would need the furnace he has decided not to light. He is the fastest refiner in the record. He has refined nothing. The whole of his working life is spent on the part of himself that costs nothing, which is also the part that can never be entered on any roll anywhere as a claim.
history: He was bound to the line's ledger before he was cold, which for an emberblood is a real disadvantage and for the household is an asset with a short fuse.
He found the intent-reading young and told nobody for eleven years, on the reasoning that the people who would pay for it would also want to own it.
The first time he said a sentence about a stranger's shoulders he was put out of a queue and had to explain himself to the field clerk, and he has not made that mistake inside a ring since.
He worked out from the record alone that lighting the furnace closes the mind path, asked nobody, and has never mentioned having worked it out.

He refused the one invitation that would have let him be examined for the condition rather than for the gift, and the refusal is the only thing about him his household has ever recorded as a decision.

personality.summary: The fastest thing in the setting at a job that requires him to be nobody, who has made being nobody a discipline rather than a defeat.

relationships.note: Fastest refinement in the record, lifespan in decades, and a mind path that closes the moment the furnace is lit, which makes the door one-way.
A line that binds every child to a named debt before first breath, whose second recorded body runs hot enough to make the household's own arithmetic expensive.
On a tier that writes elemental law the same affinity works; on the two that do not, it runs at full strength and achieves nothing at all.
The first ground in the setting where fire is simply fire, and the only place the asymmetry stops being an asymmetry.
Same technique, opposite result, and a supply line that belongs to nobody; he is on the wrong side of it, and the reason is the one he will not pay.
A fire-affinity population burning its own reserve for ten years produced bodies no other reader could classify, which made the shortage of expertise worse than the shortage of food.

reference_stats.summary: A body built to burn itself for speed, holding its one irreversible choice shut and spending the rest of its life on the part of itself that costs nothing and cannot be entered anywhere as a claim.
strengths: reads intent at the speed of a struck match, which makes him the earliest warning any office in the setting can obtain
refines faster than any body on record, so any discipline he ever opened would go further and faster than the doctrine expects
cannot be slowed by status or by cold, because his heat is drawn from nothing outside the body
weaknesses: a lifespan in decades, and a body already past the middle of it
the reserve is the body and nothing can top a body up, so there is no recovery anywhere in his condition
lighting the furnace closes the mind path for good, which is why his only doorway is one-way
his own affinity is worth nothing on this tier, and this is the tier he lives on
reference_stats.combat_read: Enormous for as long as he stays out of a fire, and not survivable in one. Fast enough to end most exchanges before they are decided, and he will lose anything that lasts longer than a body's worth of reserve, because he has no second wind and nothing in him to draw one from. Against anything he cannot anticipate he is still the fastest thing on the tier, because the intent-reading is free and does not require the furnace he has never lit.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is the species' own and it is anatomical rather than invented: the fire that refines is the fire that is paid for out of the tissue, and the fire that is lit to refine closes the mind path. Advantage and cost are one continuous process. No mechanical rule has been added here that the setting's authority on his species does not already state. Its figures about his rate and his span are authored elsewhere and are deliberately not reproduced as numbers, because this block describes a character and does not compute one.

identity.realm: None seated, and it is worth being exact, because the flattering reason would be wrong. Nothing in his structure refuses a gate: his species has no ceiling and no gate that has ever turned one away. He is unaffiliated because his species is the setting's only durable memory, and that memory turns over at about a percent a year, so the record of anything he did is gone inside a decade while the doing of it is not. A rung in this ladder is a claim made to whoever comes next. He cannot make one twice, and cannot make the first one twice either.

canon.role_in_story: A currency in this setting can be a figure nobody writes down, held in the head of exactly one member of a counting house, and it buys that house its independence because a house with nothing written has nothing to seize. He holds one. The house has been independent for four generations and the independence has been paid for in him. What makes him the right holder and the wrong one at the same time is his species: his qi is stored in bone that turns over at about a percent a year, which is what makes a memory held in him a record nobody else can edit or burn, and which is also what makes that record the only one in the setting with an expiry date on it. He is the only person here certain to outlive his own memory, and the currency he holds has no medium but a remembered figure. He is unaffiliated because a rung in any ladder in this setting is a claim made to whoever comes next, and he has never once been able to make the same claim twice.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at a house's counting table with his good hand flat on a page he has not written on, being asked by a visiting broker what the standing weight of the quarter's households was last spring, giving a figure, and then, when the broker asked him to write it down, closing the page and saying that writing it down would make it a thing the broker could carry away and a thing he could not take back.
canon.lore:
A longmarrow is a population that traded every other adaptation for lifespan. Its qi is stored in bone marrow that turns over at roughly a percent a year, and because nothing in its structure obstructs anything, there is no ceiling and no gate that has ever refused one. It cannot take the body path, because hardening the bone stops the turnover the qi depends on, which is the long joke of the species: the longest-lived body in the record is built out of the one material it may never stop replacing. Its senses are slow and deep, and given four centuries one longmarrow reaches an acuity of pattern that is not supernatural at all, only patiently arrived at. It cannot fight, it knows it cannot fight, and it is organised as knowledge rather than as force.

That is the species. The trouble is the medium, and the setting has already written the trouble down inside the archive practice itself. The Long Marrow Memory is the only durable library here: a memory held in marrow can be neither edited nor burned by anybody else. It cannot be copied either. A holder's death is not a copy being retired; it is the only copy being retired. Four centuries of one archive is the largest single loss per person this setting has ever suffered, and the population is valued accordingly.

Nobody wrote down the other half. The turnover rate is a percent a year, which is what makes the practice possible and also what makes the loss total, and the same rate that keeps a memory safe from other hands keeps it safe from itself. What he holds decays. Not quickly, and not in any way you would notice inside a conversation: a figure from nine years ago is gone, a sequence from thirty is gone, a judgement he is entirely capable of forming is gone once he has formed it, because forming it used up the tissue that held the previous one. Nothing his species has ever built survived to be inherited intact. The limitation sits entirely downstream of the success.

So the currency he holds has the safest and the shortest-lived medium in the setting. He is its one issuer, by an arrangement with no marker at all, because a marker would convert an invisible authority into a visible office anybody could apply for. It cannot be taught faster than it can be learned. Nothing can be lent into it and nothing can be taken out. And a house that loses one person loses its currency entirely. He has been the holder for thirty-one years and expects to be the holder for three hundred more, and somewhere in the middle of that stretch the figures he is holding will have gone and he will still be the only person alive entitled to say what they were.

That is why he is unaffiliated, and it has nothing to do with his ability. Nothing in his body refuses anything. The reason is that a rung in this setting is a claim, and a claim must be checkable by whoever comes after the person who made it, and the only medium available to him is one that does not survive to be checked. He would be, in the phrase this setting uses about bodies like his, a cultivator whose attainment nobody afterwards could certify. He has declined to be that, and the refusal has cost him the one thing his species is actually for.

What he does instead is the part of the office that does not expire in a single season: he answers. Four centuries of one subject is a discipline in itself. A question put to him about a house's dealings in any decade of his holding gets a straight answer, and a question about a figure from a decade ago gets the truth, which is that there is none. That second answer is the most valuable thing the house can receive and the one no broker has ever wanted.
history: He was bound to a house's count while the line's previous holder was still alive and still able to check him, which the arrangement forbids and which happened exactly once.
The first time a figure he had given went missing he assumed he had mislaid it, and established nine years later that the bone holding it was simply not the bone he had been using.
He stopped writing anything down in his twenty-fourth year as holder, on the reasoning that a written figure can be cited and an unverified one can only be believed.

The house survived a raid that took the books, the ink and the counterweights and lost nothing that mattered, which is the whole argument for the office and the reason he was made to give out the entire day's figures from memory afterwards as a demonstration.

He was offered a place on a school roster by somebody who wanted to learn a technique, declined, and gave the reason in one sentence that the offerer repeated back to him as though it were a figure of speech.

reference_stats.combat_read: He is not a fighter and has never been one: light, fragile to force, extraordinarily difficult to exhaust. A long engagement is the worst shape for him because it outlasts both his patience and his body. Against anything that must be worn down by a single effort he is close to untouchable, and against anything that arrives all at once he is a hundred and forty pounds of bone with no muscle and a lifetime of never having needed one.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is his species' own anatomy and not an invented rule: the same turnover that makes a memory in him unburnable makes it unlasting. identity.realm: None seated. Her species closes nothing: every path is open to her and her ceiling is the eleventh, inherited from a salt parent and unchanged by a watered one, so range is not power and she has never mistaken it. She is unaffiliated because her species has no native ground at all. It needs a shoreline, and a shoreline is contested ground, so she is the one body in the setting enrolled nowhere by default, and enrolment in this setting is an entry against a place. She has been entered three times and cancelled three times at the next reconciliation of the ground against the roll.

canon.role_in_story: The gate on this tier sells standing at the field and keeps a list of places rather than a list of names, because the seats are resold continuously and the only thing anybody needs proved afterwards is who paid. It is also the only tax the plains can actually collect. It works because passage is the one supply chain whose unit is a person, because nobody may levy a seat, and because a crossing is a thing you can be sold twice. She is the best crossing in the region: the only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, so she can take a message from the salt side to the water side in one trip and arrive able to drink where she lands. She is also the one person on the shore the gate's own book cannot hold. It files places, and she has none, because her species has no native ground and needs a shoreline, which is the one piece of ground two households own in the same hour.
canon.first_appearance: First seen on the far bank of the rift with a sealed tin in one hand and a tide mark on her knee, telling a gate clerk that she could not say which side she had started from, and then adding, unasked for, that she had now said that three times at three different desks and that every one of them had entered her anyway.
canon.lore:
A brinecaller is the only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, and it exists because both of its parents are trapped by their own element: one cannot leave the pan and the other cannot leave the water. The cross is the single biological answer to being trapped twice, and the answer turned out to be a merchant, which is why the crossing spread along trade routes rather than across them. Its anatomy is a saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a watered parent's sensory apparatus, and its kidney reads two chemistries at once. Its senses are the best chemical sense in the record by a wide margin, because it must tell two kinds of water apart at a glance and is always being lied to by one of them. Its soul and meridian set are perfectly legible and structurally neither parent. Its ceiling is the eleventh, inherited from the salt parent and unchanged by the water one, so the cross widened the species' range without raising its power: range is not power. And its refinement is noticeably slower than either parent in that parent's own medium, which is the cross's actual cost and the sentence the setting uses to close the subject.

The cost the record does not put in the same paragraph is the one that has decided her life. Her species is nowhere native. It needs a shoreline, and a shoreline is contested ground.

Everything in this setting that writes a person down files them against a place, and every place in it is somebody's: a household keeps a roll of its own, a street keeps one, a quarter keeps one, a settlement reconciles its roll against its ground at a count and the ground wins. She is enrolled nowhere by default. There is no household on either bank whose roll contains her, because she belongs to the crossing and not to a side of it, and the crossing has no roll. Where she has stayed longest, the ground has moved under her twice and the roll has been reconciled twice and both times she has come out of the reconciliation as a figure that does not net out. She was entered three times. Two of those were at the gate, whose book is a list of places, and the third was at a household that wanted the name on its book for a winter. All three were withdrawn by arithmetic at the next count. Nobody refused her. There was a line, and the line was correct, and then the ground said otherwise.

So she is unaffiliated, and the reason is not the ladder. The ladder is open to her at every rung her species can reach and she has never touched one. The reason is that a path in this setting is not a thing a body does; it is a thing a body is entered as, and the entry is an assertion about where somebody belongs, and she has never in her life belonged anywhere that would survive being written down.

What she does with that is the thing she is actually for. Two houses cannot settle an account between them here, because neither will state a figure, so every cross-house settlement is done by weight, by inspection, or by standing name. She is the inspection. She walks both chemistries in a season and comes back with what each side's water actually weighs, which is the only evidence in the setting that a substitution has happened and the only reading neither house can produce for itself. Her verdict is as good as anybody's and completely unattributable: put her in the record and it cannot be said which bank she was standing on when she made it. She has settled eleven such disputes and is named in none of them, and the standing name she has been offered in place of a figure would be the one thing in this arrangement she cannot take.
history: She was the first of her line on this shore and the reason the crossing spread here at all, because the crossing spread along trade and she was trade.

Her first household on the salt side put her on the roll for a winter and the winter's count withdrew her, because the ground she was counted against had been re-cut in a flood and her line belonged to neither bank of the new channel.

She worked out, on her second crossing season, that the gate's book is a list of places, and that a body without a place cannot be entered in it at all, and started using that as an argument with brokers who had been overcharging for her crossings.

The third cancellation came at a desk where the clerk entered her anyway on the strength of her own account of having been born two valleys over, which was true and which was on the wrong side of the water.
She has since been offered a standing name in place of a figure and has declined it, on the grounds that a name is a place and she has already refused three of those.

reference_stats.combat_read: She is not built for a fight and knows it: a saltfolk frame gone gracile, with no muscle to speak of and a ceiling of eleven inherited rather than reached. On open ground between two waters she is very difficult to corner, because she can drink and run on either side and nobody can herd her across a single chemist's line. Once cornered on one chemistry she is a soft body above that chemist's ceiling, and the sensible answer for her is never to be standing still on either bank for long enough for a question about her to become a question about her position.

The advantage and the cost are the two halves of one crossing, and the only institution named here is described by its own attributes rather than given rules it does not have. shots.framing: diagrammatic elevation of the channel with the figure duplicated and no ground line drawn under either copy

shots.scene: the rift channel at mid-tide, the crossing she makes twice a season and nobody else makes at all
shots.pose: one figure crossing a channel far wider than the frame, the far bank out of reach
shots.expression: too far to read; the intent is scale and the distance her species can cross and nobody else can
shots.framing: wide from the salt bank, the figure small and the water carrying the whole picture

shots.scene: the water-side bank of the same rift, the crossing seen from the side she is not entered on
shots.pose: the same channel from the other bank with the salt crust in the foreground and the weed behind
shots.expression: too far to read; the second bank is a different chemistry and the picture says so by colour alone
shots.framing: high and slightly behind, looking down the bank at the water and the crossing laid out flat

shots.scene: the salt bank with a flood coming up behind her and both chemistries within reach of a single sprint
shots.pose: turning on the bank with the tin high and one knee already off the slope, running the wrong way downhill on purpose
shots.expression: no expression; the picture is about a body leaving rather than about a body fighting
shots.framing: low and wide from the water's edge, the figure breaking out of the frame at the corner

shots.scene: a cross-house settlement, the inspection both sides asked for and neither of them can produce
shots.pose: at a long table with two seated figures either side of her and a single unlit weight scale between them
shots.expression: no face; both houses are represented by hands kept off the one instrument on the table
shots.framing: side-on at the edge of frame, half the picture given to the scale and the hands not touching it

shots.scene: a gate desk, giving her account of a valley she was born in
shots.pose: standing at a desk with one hand already on the rail, ready to be entered somewhere
shots.expression: ready, the expression of somebody about to give a clerk what the clerk wants
shots.framing: close and square, the desk edge cropping the picture at the bottom

shots.scene: a gate desk, the third time being told the entry would be reconciled
shots.pose: the same stance with the hand off the rail and the forearm wiped across the wrist
shots.expression: withdrawn, having heard the desk's question before the desk has asked it
shots.framing: slightly wider, the whole upper body in frame and the desk behind her

shots.scene: the upper track above the shore, the one route her senses give her nothing on
shots.pose: head turned uphill away from the water, which is the one direction she does not face willingly
shots.expression: suspicious of a cliff path, which is the only thing on this coast she cannot read
shots.framing: over the shoulder from behind, the head turned far enough that only the jaw and one wet sleeve show

shots.scene: the ford, a season's samples lifted out and counted before she has dried off
shots.pose: hauling a heavy tin out of the water with both arms and one knee in the channel
shots.expression: physical effort and no complaint, the face of a body used to being the only way round
shots.framing: low from the waterline, the figure half in the frame and the spray carrying the rest

shots.scene: the stone above the ford, an hour between crossings with the boots drying
shots.pose: sitting on the stone above the tideline with her boots off and her feet bleeding slowly
shots.expression: tired and specific, the tiredness of a crossing repeated rather than of anything else
shots.framing: level and close, a private hour with no second party in it

shots.scene: a household's winter count, the third withdrawal of the same name
shots.pose: standing in front of a house's roll with her name not on it and her arms loose at her sides
shots.expression: formal and slightly amused, the face of a woman declining a line she has already been given three times
shots.framing: tight on the upper body, the roll visible behind her shoulder and her hands well away from it

shots.scene: a cross-house settlement, giving a figure by weight because by figure is not available
shots.pose: half-turned with one hand out flat over the table, indicating a weight rather than a place
shots.expression: helpful to a precision her senses have and the table does not
shots.framing: high and slightly behind, looking down at the scale and the two pairs of hands kept off it

shots.scene: the ford, a flood she was caught on the wrong side of, read the way she reads water
shots.pose: holding her forearm up to a lamp and reading the white line along it
shots.expression: unguarded and specific, the face of somebody reading a mark her own body made
shots.framing: half-profile, half the picture given to the arm and the line on it rather than to her face

shots.scene: the shore, the crossing done and both accounts closed and her name in neither
shots.pose: still on the bank with the channel going down in front of her and the light going with it
shots.expression: quietly pleased at a settlement she made that neither house has had to appeal
shots.framing: a long lens along the water, the figure small and centred on the near bank

shots.scene: the rift channel at mid-tide, the crossing between the two chemistries
shots.pose: the crossing: mid-channel with the tin held high and the current breaking around her thighs
shots.expression: the face of a body doing the only thing it was made for
shots.framing: medium three-quarter at working distance, the ordinary hour doing most of the frame

shots.scene: the salt bank's tide line, the substitution nobody else can taste
shots.pose: the reading: crouched at the tideline with two fingers in the water and her head over them
shots.expression: the face of a woman who can tell two waters apart at a glance
shots.framing: side-on at the edge of frame, half the picture given to the water she is reading

shots.scene: the sea wall above the ford, the one descent her body is always asking her to take
shots.pose: the descent: facing the channel with her back to the whole of the salt bank and the sea wall behind
shots.expression: the face of somebody deliberately going the wrong way downhill
shots.framing: wide from a doorway in the sea wall, the figure mid-turn and unaware of being looked at

shots.scene: a cross-house settlement, the inspection both sides asked for
shots.pose: the weighing: standing square to a table with both palms flat on it and the scale between two houses' hands
shots.expression: the face of a woman who is the instrument and knows it
shots.framing: level and close, a private moment with a second party who is not in the frame

shots.scene: the stone above the ford, the hour the water has to drop before the far bank is walkable
shots.pose: the waiting: on a stone above the water with her knees up and the tin beside her, watching the channel
shots.expression: the face of somebody waiting on a tide rather than on a person
shots.framing: waist-up at rest between tasks, hands occupied by nothing, nothing performed

shots.scene: a gate desk, a standing name offered in place of a figure
shots.pose: the refusal: standing at a desk with her forearms crossed over the page, refusing to sign a standing name
shots.expression: the face of a woman declining the one thing that would fix her to a bank
shots.framing: high and slightly behind, looking down at the page and the clerk's pen

shots.scene: the shore above the rift ford, at first light, before the day's work has properly begun: the samples smelled before they are weighed, because the nose settles a question the scale only confirms
shots.pose: on the salt bank with the first light off the crust, checking yesterday's samples by smell before she checks them by weight
shots.expression: absorbed, the expression of someone counting
shots.framing: along the salt crust at ankle height, the tideline crossing the picture behind her

shots.scene: the rift channel, in the middle of the working day, at its least remarkable: the second crossing of the week with nothing to report
shots.pose: mid-channel with the current at her waist and the tin on her shoulder
shots.expression: unguarded and mid-thought, no one to perform for
shots.framing: side-on at the edge of frame, half the picture given to the water rather than to her

shots.scene: the sea wall above the ford, at the day's end, the accounts closed and the hour hers
shots.pose: sitting on the sea wall with her feet in the run-off and the ledger open beside her, not reading it
shots.expression: flat with fatigue, nothing being concealed and nothing being said
shots.framing: wide from a doorway, the figure mid-routine and unaware of being looked at

shots.scene: the water-side bank, after dark, by whatever light the work can be done by: the tide called off a lamp because the second bank cannot have one lit on it
shots.pose: on the water-side bank with a lamp held low over the channel, checking which way the tide is setting
shots.expression: quietly pleased at a small competent thing, which is a tide she called correctly an hour ago
shots.framing: low and wide, the figure against the one lamp rather than posed to it
